utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For the sake of the record, could we have the appearances, please. Yes, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Peter McCloskey, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence of Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Mr. Prosecutor. I am Miodrag Stojanovic, Defence counsel for Mr. Jokic. And together with me at this pre-Defence conference is my colleague, co-counsel, Branko Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence of Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Michael Karnavas. Good afternoon, Mr. President, Judge Vassylenko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is a pre-Defence conference held in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The purpose of this conference is to help the Defence counsel of Mr. Jokic to prepare his case, which I believe will start on the 2nd of July with the opening statement by his counsel. There are several issues in my agenda; the first one is about the witness list, the second is about a special witness which might have the videolink and we might go into private session whenever we talk about those witnesses, the third issue is about exhibits, the fourth, opening statement; the fifth, Rule 84 bis statement; the sixth, other issues. Let's deal with those matters one by one. The first is about the 65 ter filings by the Defence of Mr. Jokic. The Defence counsel filed the 65 ter filing on the 18th of March, 2004, in which they ask for about 13 witnesses to be heard by this Bench in their case. And generally speaking, this Bench is not quite satisfied with those filings because we lack some specific information about the testimony of those witnesses. And it made it a little bit difficult to deal with the witness matters. But anyway, like in the pre-Defence conference for the defence of Mr. Blagojevic, we would like to go over the witness list one by one. And I will refer the number instead of name of those witnesses. If there is a need, we'll go into private session. But the purpose is that at this stage we will not disclose the identity and names of those potential witnesses. As first witness, I believe that we need some additional information. As for the first issue, this Bench believes that the testimony of those -- this witness is only relevant as mitigating circumstances because we heard the testimony of some witnesses in the Prosecution's case. It seems to me that there is no disputes about it. Am I right, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, if we're talking about in the first paragraphs the assistance of boys crossing. I have no evidence to indicate that -- to dispute that. And of course the next line about the witnesses relate to the overall context of combat activities, I don't know what that really means, of course, except that the movement of the column, the activity of the -- all the armies and aside from some specific issues that we're aware of, there's not really a lot of conflict with that. And the rules relating to the duty operations officers, yes, we've heard a lot about that and I don't think there's been a whole lot of conflict about what those rules are, but hearing it from the Muslim side may have something that the Court has some value in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. As the second issue, I think the second part is too broad. It's very difficult for us to understand how relevant this testimony is. At this stage, we do not ask the Defence counsel to give us a very detailed explanation, but at least you should tell us what is that overall context of the combat activities, whether those activities related to your client or not, because we have heard a lot of evidence before already. And as for the third part, third segment of his testimony, we believe that, reading from the 65 ter filings, this part is somehow overlapped with the witness 2. So I need some explanations from Mr. Stojanovic, but not into the very specific details. Just give us a rough idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I hope that we are now in private session, or perhaps I'm not going to mention any names. Perhaps I'll just give numbers, because witness number 1 is the only one who asked for protective measures while giving evidence; whereas, for the others there's no problem in terms of mentioning their names. So I'll just refer to witness number 1 as witness number 1. In our 65 ter filings, we indicated what this witness would testify about. We wish to make it clear to the Court what the general context was of combat activities on those days, the 14th, 15th, and 16th of July in the area of defence of the Zvornik Brigade and from a completely different angle at that, the angle of the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And as a matter of fact, on the part of an officer who at that point from an operations point of view held the highest position at the 2nd -- at the forward command post of the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In addition to that, when hearing this witness we would like the Trial Chamber to see how intensive the combat activities were and how engaged the respective forces of the two armies were. And finally, in that context, to describe the events that we thought would be a mitigating circumstance, namely we wanted him to speak about the character of our client. We would like to avail ourselves of another opportunity. Since this witness lived and worked in Zvornik in 1990 and in 1991, we would like him to say what he knew then about Dragan Jokic, our client, and also about a series of information that he had received from members of the BH army who were ethnic Muslims, Bosniaks, and this information has to do with our client, Dragan Jokic. Finally, it is important for us to take advantage of his presence in order to tender the documents that we asked for and that we received in part from the federal ministry of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that on that day the 16th of July, 1995, were taken or confiscated from the vehicle that Dragan Obrenovic used on that day. We believe that a view from the other side of the combat line of a high-ranking officer of the BH army would be invaluable assistance to the Trial Chamber to, quite simply, understand the gravity of everything that happened and the historical context of those days, the four days that are most relevant to the indictment as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And you stated here in that document saying that estimated duration of testimony, one trial day, you mean the direct examination only or including the cross-examination? As you know, the principle in our proceedings is normally one day/one witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Those were the dynamics of witness examination that we relied on for four weeks. And that is what we provided the Prosecution with, too. According to those dynamics, we expected to hear this witness on one day, namely Monday, the 12th of July, in direct examination, and on Tuesday, the 13th of July, 2004, the witness would be cross-examined. That is the preliminary schedule that we made on the basis of your instructions and the time allotted to us. And we have provided the Prosecution with a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you. I hope we could do the direct examination and cross-examination in one day, because judging from the contents this witness is going to tell us, there is nothing, if I may say, directly related to the conducts of your client. He's talking about the overall context of the combat activities, talking about the rules which we have heard a lot. So I think there is still a possibility to shorten the length of the direct examination and more generally speaking, we'll stick to the principle that one day/one witness. Thank you. As for the second witness, we have no questions, no objections. But as for the third witness, we have some problems. Maybe we could go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We are now in open session. As witness 4 and 5 are -- I'm sorry, as witness 4, we have no problem. As witness 5, we need additional information, because we couldn't get any useful information from those 65 ter filings. And the -- as for the witness number 6, well, I don't know about the relevance of the testimony of this witness because they're talking about something in 1992 rather than in 1995. Maybe if we finish all the list. As for the witness number 7, we have no difficulties. Number 8, no difficulties. Number 9, we need -- well, let's talk about witness number 8. The number 8 witness I believe is a character witness, which does not -- whose testimony does not go into directly the conducts of the accused during that particular period. So we believe that as a 92 bis witness, that is enough because it only goes to the mitigating factors. Witness number 9, we need the additional information. Witness number 10, yes, no problem. Witness number 11, we also need the additional information. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. First, let me go back to witness number 5. I think that's the first witness I need to say more about. This is a man who was a member of the engineers company of the Zvornik Brigade, and he was in the pioneers' squad, as they call it, in the pioneers' platoon. In his private life, he is a land surveyor. And in the period of time covered by the indictment, he participated in the activities of this unit. He will first speak about the structure of the engineers' company, about the way command and control was exercised over this company, about who he received orders from. He will also testify about the position of Dragan Jokic as the chief of engineers and the relationship between the komandir or company leader, the komandir or leader of the platoon that the witness belonged to, the chief of the engineers, and the brigade commander. He will further testify about an event that occurred, and he cannot recall this precisely, either on the 17th or the 18th of July when he and Dragan Jokic were given a task to carry out together. He will testify as to where Dragan Jokic was on the 17th and what activities they engaged in. And this is all connected to the testimony of witness number 1. Your Honours, we have envisioned that this witness's testimony should last for an hour, and we have linked his testimony to the testimony of witness number 7, who at that time was the komandir of the engineers' company. And we plan to have these two witnesses testify for one day. In our estimation, it would be important for our defence to convince the Chamber as to how the engineers' company was commanded and what the position of Dragan Jokic was with respect to the statements or the allegations in the indictment, because wherever engineers are mentioned in the indictment, Dragan Jokic's name is linked to them. If you agree, I may continue. Shall I go on to talk about the other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, but please be as concise as possible, because we are expecting a supplementary filings concerning with the 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In any case, we will explain it all because there are some changes. The person under number 6, we have taken him off our witness list because the period he testified about is not relevant, but we felt that he would be useful as a military expert. We will talk about this later. Witness number 9, Your Honours, was a professor in the school of economics, and he was the treasurer in the brigade. He is one of the men who on the 14th of July went to Orahovac to stand guard where the prisoners were. Witness P130 identified him as one of the persons who arrived from the command of the Zvornik Brigade after he had completed a conversation with the duty officer in the Zvornik Brigade. This witness will testify about how it came about that he went to Orahovac to stand guard, what he saw in Orahovac, and who sent him to Orahovac. This witness has already made a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, and he does not mention Dragan Jokic's name in all this. In our view, this is of importance in order to prove Dragan Jokic's position on the 14th of July. Finally, witness number 11 will testify about the events that took place in the village of Pilica, the Pilica cultural centre, and the Branjevo Military Farm. On the 14th, he was an eyewitness of an event, and he testifies about the role of Pero Petrovic, a Prosecution witness who, if you remember, testified here saying that because there were no telephone connections between Pilica and Zvornik, he went to the neighbouring village, called the duty officer, and he thinks it was Dragan Jokic. He asked about the prisoners, and the duty officer said they were military prisoners and that he should go home. We also intend to introduce some exhibits through this witness compromising the statement of Pero Petrovic and his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we come to the witnesses 12 and 13. As I understand, these two witnesses are proposed as expert witnesses. But if they are the expert witnesses, what we need is, first, the establishment of his status as an expert. We need resumes, including the -- any publishings in these fields. Secondly, we need the statements of those two witnesses. Are there any statements and when are you going to furnish it with the other party as well as to the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We are aware of our obligation and we only wanted to inform you that we propose to remove from our preliminary list the names under numbers 12 and 13 and to have a military expert. And we propose that this be the witness that was previously under number 6. This is an expert who was a colonel in the Army of Serbia and Montenegro from the engineers, and he's a very important expert. I asked him to compile a report describing the duties of the duty operations officer and the chief of engineers according to the rules that were in force in 1995. I also asked him to deal with the issue of mobilising engineers machinery. Today, we have his CV, which we have submitted to the registry asking that he be appointed a military expert. And his opinion and his report, which will be about 35 pages long, will be submitted to the Court and the OTP on the 26th of this month. We would therefore be in compliance with the 30-day period required prior to this witness's testimony. We propose that he be heard on the 28th, the 29th, and the 30th of July, and this would be both the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination. This expert's task would be to deal with the competences and authority of the duty operations officer as well as the position, powers, and duties of the chief of engineers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. And we are eager to see your revised 65 ter filings. I hope those amendments will be incorporated in your filings. As for the specific date of hearing this witness, you really want us to sit until the last day before the summer is ended? Well, as for the last witness which did not appear on the 65 ter filings, that is the request for subpoenas. I think this Trial Chamber made an order and asked for the additional informations. So would you please tell us, are you going to file that additional information with us, including what efforts your team has made to call him? You don't have to go into the details, because if you filed that or if you are going to file that information, eventually we'll read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may we go into private session for only a few minutes so that we can inform you as to what we have done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, as you requested, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the next issue is about the exhibits the Defence is going to use in their case. We believe that the Defence should submit their exhibit list to the Trial Chamber and the parties this week, by Friday, the 25th of June, pursuant to Rule 65 ter (G)(i) with copies of proposed exhibits to the Prosecution by Monday, 28th June. Mr. Stojanovic, did you prepare that exhibit list that you are going to use in your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, there will not be a large number of exhibits. We have about ten new exhibits we intend to use. And for the most part, we shall be using the documents seized in the Zvornik Brigade, which are in the collection of documents disclosed to us by the Prosecution. By Friday, we shall inform both you and the Office of the Prosecutor about these documents. Your Honours, by your leave, I wish to add that we have prepared another four witnesses on this list, which we shall submit as an amended list, whom we propose to call viva voce. I can tell you very briefly now who these witnesses are and what this is about, although I have already informed the Prosecutor about this. Because we have taken those two witnesses off the list, and now we have these further four witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, as a matter of fact, the Defence could call, as a principle, as many witnesses as they could, so long as we can finish the testimony of those witnesses within, within, the time period that the Bench granted to you and so long as the testimony of those witnesses is relevant to this case. I will be very reluctant to ask you to cut the -- cut short the list of witnesses or add more witnesses on the lists either. But so long as you could finish the testimony of those witnesses within the requested period, I think you have the discretion to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This will certainly be within the time limit you have set. And we may not even use all this time. But we have planned it in such a way that there will be sufficient time, both for us and the Prosecution to examine Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next issue is about the opening statement. I believe that Mr. Stojanovic, you mentioned that you present your opening statement on Friday, 2nd July. Could I ask how long do you think that statement will last?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I have already started working on it, and I think that I will be speaking for a little under two sessions, that is for about two hours and a quarter. I have seven arguments to make, and also I wish to draw a picture of the general context, the position of the Zvornik Brigade, and the position of Dragan Jokic in all these events. So two hours and a quarter at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And another issue is the Rule 84 bis statement. I would like to know, Mr. Stojanovic, whether your client would like to make a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have had a long discussion with our client about this. It was one of the most difficult issues that we have dealt with in these two years. However, I still cannot give you a definite reply, but we have not put him on the witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you have to distinguish the statement and the witness in his case; that's two different issues. So at this moment, you could not give me an answer? Yes, I hope that just in case, if your witness -- your client would like to make a statement or would like to be a witness in his case, please inform us as early as possible, just in case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, are there any other issues that the parties would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But not in relation to this hearing, this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me hear about anything related to this hearing first, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. It seems to me there's none. Yes, let's deal with the other matters, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a short matter. This afternoon I was handed four statements, witness statements. They're dated 24th of May, 25th of May. One is an interview that took place 22nd and 25th of May, and the other one the 24th of May. In looking at the statements, it would appear that not only were they taken on those days but they are signed on those particular days as well. Now, I don't know whether in fact they were typed on those days and signed on those days. It's rather unclear, but it would appear that because on each page there is a date. And at the end of each statement - these are not tape recorded statements - so at the end there is a witness acknowledgment with a signature and a date. The statements, not all of them, but at least three of the four are rather significant in my opinion. And my question is: Why has it taken close to a month -- I guess, over a month or close to a month, give a day or two, for these statements to be provided to us? Because obviously, there's -- perhaps we would have liked to have had this information, to check it, and see whether we needed to add anybody to our list. It comes virtually at the end of our case. And I can understand if they had to have long translations and what have you. But here again, it would appear that they were typed on the day that they were taken, so we have one month in storage before they're being submitted to us. So I would like an explanation because I think if no adequate explanation can be given, I must lodge some sort of a protest, because I think I then have to look at this and see whether I need additional time for my case, but I don't know yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I know next to nothing about those statements and did you have a chance to discuss it with the party?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just received them and I've been reading them while we've been doing this hearing as well. And I just want to go -- I want an answer on the record, Your Honour, because if they were taken on the 25th and typed on the 25th and they were signed on the 25th or the 22nd of May, why am I getting them today? Why didn't I get them back then? I mention this only because with respect to witness 130, you know, the -- this rather important witness, as soon as they learned of certain information, we were told about it. So on that instance, there was very prompt notice. Here it seems there's a 30-day delay. I don't know the reasons, but I certainly would like them on the record because I feel that perhaps something is awry over here. Maybe it just fell through the cracks. I'm willing to accept any explanation, but I would like an explanation on the record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have anything to say to this man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Karnavas raised this issue in open court and so our knowledge, we know next to nothing object those statements at all, about this matter. And maybe you could assist us to understand the situation rather than directly answer any questions put by Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He has plenty of time to discuss this with me, Mr. President. He's doing this in order to be able to make his insinuations in his continuing effort to demean the Prosecution. You know, why he feels a need to do this? I'm about at the end of my rope with it. I don't need to explain myself to Mr. Karnavas or to anyone else. And this is -- it's just -- because you have asked me, and of course I will, but the problem we have here is that encouraging this kind of activity only allows it to go on and on and on. Had it not been -- had he just asked what it's about, I wouldn't have had a problem. But all the insinuations that there's something suspicious going on, it's hard to get up day by day with that constant insinuation and allegation and deal with it and just pretend that it's not going on, especially late in the day after having heard a dose of it in court today, but I will. We went on a mission. When you go on a mission to Bosnia, it takes usually a few days to get back from the mission after you've done things. Everything is in the computer. When an investigator gets back from a mission, sometimes he goes on holiday, sometimes he's able to get to work. Usually he's got a tonne of e-mails and other things he has to respond to, issues come up, they run around. Getting a report, series of reports, done and typed up and reviewed by the supervisor and back within 30 days isn't bad. And if I get the word from someone that there's something very important out there, I try to always give everyone the word, the heads up on it, because that's the way I work. This material came to my desk a few days ago, and it took me a day or two to look at it to see if it was discoverable material, what it was about. So then I gave it to him. And of course I would have told this to Mr. Karnavas had he asked me. I would have said it in open court had he asked it in a civilised way. But I apologise for my lack of patience, Your Honour, but that's the story.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just received this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It has a date --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just received it just this afternoon, as I walked in. It has a date 22nd June, 2004. Now, what is suspicious to me - and I'm just saying suspicious - every page has a date on it and every page has an initial. And so it would appear that in the field these were typed. I don't know, but that's what it would appear because otherwise how can they take the statement on the 25th of May, have it tape recorded -- have it typed, and then have signatures on each page. That's what I'm stating. As far as Mr. Bursik going, coming back and reading e-mails, cry me a river. That's my approach because we are in the middle of a trial right now. We are in the middle of the Defence case. That's not my excuse. I'm not blaming Mr. McCloskey. I'm just asking for explanation. I don't see why he's getting so upset at me; I really don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey is standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When they come back in the computer, if they were initialled, they possibly -- we don't do anything with them until there what's called IFF-ed or MIFF-ed [sic] or something, which means they have to be given these ERN numbers that you see. So there's a process by which each document gets slightly summarised by another document, and that goes into the system, sometimes there's foul-ups and it takes a while. We've learned over the years that we really need to do this so we try to avoid the few times where we've seen things that have slipped through the cracks without these numbers. There are reasons. 30 days is not bad. I don't know, again, what the problem is that except that this is continually dramatics on the part of the Defence. That's what's involved in this and I think Mr. Karnavas knows there's no sleight of hand. What is the suspicions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not saying anything. I'm not accusing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not accusing him of anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, let me say a few words. I think if there's any requests made by the parties, before that the parties have to make the situation clear, which might request the consultations or meetings between the parties. If still there is some problem existing and if one party feels their legitimate right was prejudiced against, they could inform the Bench as soon as possible and we will see what we could do. I hope in the future we should follow this kind of practice. Yes. Yes, Mr. Blagojevic. I saw you are raising your hands long before, but we have to deal with one thing after another.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that, Your Honour, and I thank you for giving me the opportunity to say something, as I will right now. Please, I am saying this for the sake of the transcript, because I really don't know what awaits me tomorrow. I will try to be under control and not to say something I shouldn't. It has to do with witness V3. I think I understood what this is all about. Since I heard very different positions over a very short span of time, and I am truly concerned about that because I don't know what's behind it, for example this discussion just now where it was said a few minutes ago that there was a high degree of concurrence, that is -- I'm really concerned about it. I'm addressing you, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll consider the submissions by the parties, as well as by Mr. Blagojevic on this issue and try to make our decisions on this issue. So if there is nothing else, the hearing is adjourned. And tomorrow we'll continue the proceedings in Courtroom I, 9.00 in the morning. ---Whereupon the Pre-Defence Conference adjourned at 5.55 p.m.
